title: Terra API sues Garmin over who controls users' health data | Terra
summary: Terra API is suing Garmin for blocking companies from using Terra, cutting off their users' connections and blocking them from sharing their data with the apps they chose.
body_markdown:
Terra API has filed a lawsuit against Garmin in California. Garmin cut off hundreds of thousands of users from sending their own data to the apps they chose, and never answered our requests under the EU Data Act. We are going to court because the data you generate on a device belongs to you.


You can imagine this is not a decision one makes lightly. We are a startup, and they are one of the biggest wearable makers globally. It’s the absolute last thing we wanted.


But this comes down to one question.


When you wear a device, who does your data belong to?


## How we got here


A few weeks ago, I wrote how it all started.


For almost 6 years, we’ve been helping hundreds of thousands of Garmin users share their data with their favorite apps.


In September, Garmin reached out and asked us to make changes to our customer setup through their developer portal. At the same time, they blocked our ability to make the changes they asked for and stopped answering our questions.


Overnight, hundreds of thousands of people lost their ability to send their own data to the apps they chose. These were apps across coaching, research, overall health, and many more. Patients on care platforms suddenly lost the connections they depend on, too.


Nobody asked those people.


And things got even worse. Our customers reached out, saying Garmin was asking them to pay directly and sign new terms excluding third parties.


They cannot do this under the EU Data Act and GDPR Articles 5 and 20.


So we reached out to Garmin again to honor their obligations under these Acts. But it doesn't seem to matter for Garmin, since they never responded.


Since we've tried everything, we are going to court.
